claims.text: The root cause of human suffering lies in disconnection — from others, from the present moment, and from a deeper sense of unity.
Sri Preethaji teaches that when we are lost in a stressful state, we feel isolated even amidst people, and our actions become driven by agitation or rigid ideas rather than genuine compassion.
This disconnection leads to insensitivity, indifference, and even harm to those we love.
In contrast, the Beautiful State arises from connection — to others, to the present, and to a sense of inner simplicity.
Here, actions flow naturally from empathy and understanding, as seen in the monk Yesmi, who helps others not out of guilt or duty but because he feels their pain deeply.
This state brings clarity, intelligence, and decisive action, allowing us to help both ourselves and those around us.
These two states — the stressful state and the Beautiful State — shape our daily life by determining how we relate to ourselves and others.
One leads to suffering; the other to peace and compassionate action.

Human beings internally experience life from only two states: a stressful state and a beautiful, stress-free state. While external challenges constantly shape our lives, our inner condition ultimately determines our perception of reality. The same external circumstances—such as work catching up or facing constant change in the world—can be experienced entirely differently depending on whether we are in a stressful or beautiful state. This duality reveals that stress does not come from external situations themselves, but from our internal state of being. Understanding this fundamental truth is the first step toward teaching young people (and ourselves) to cultivate an ageless joy and navigate a fast-changing world without anxiety. By recognizing that we alone create our experience through our inner state, we can learn to shift from stress to the beautiful state, regardless of external circumstances.
